historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 7.9% exceeds revenue 3.2% and EPS 4.7% by >30%: book value grew because buybacks fell to ~$370-600M/yr against ~$1.5B of earnings, not because the business compounded faster. historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2019 $1,621.0M, FY2021 $1,167.6M, FY2024 $1,400.6M. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR (-2.9%) is below the reported FCF CAGR (-1.9%) because interest income rose from $60M to $101M on a larger cash pile; SBC was stable at ~0.6% of revenue. FY2022 ($848M reported) was a working-capital trough, not an operating one.

scenario_narratives.base: The integration lands roughly as guided, and a year in the evidence is on side: six creative networks became three without visible client losses, Core organic growth reached 7.2% in Q3 2026, adjusted EBITA margin expanded 200bp and the $900M 2026 synergy target was reaffirmed. From the FY2026E base, Core Operations grow 3% then 2.5% a year as a 'Big 3' scale media buyer with a data platform -- the recent 6-7% is treated as a soft-comparison and new-business bulge, not a new trend. EBITDA margin settles at 18.8% (EBITA ~18.0%) once the last cash severance, integration and exited-lease costs roll off in FY2027-28. FCF is deployed to the remaining buyback authorization and the $3.20 dividend, which the model treats as value-neutral; net interest expense near $400M a year is the carrying cost of the $10B of debt and is charged through WACC and the bridge. The axes are organic growth versus the 2-3% industry rate, synergy capture net of give-back, and whether the market's single-digit adjusted P/E persists -- the 12x FCF exit cap assumes a modest re-rating toward Omnicom's own history, not toward the market.
scenario_narratives.bull: Scale and data become a real moat: media-buying leverage against Google, Meta, Amazon and retail media networks plus Omni/Acxiom/Kinesso identity data hold organic growth at 4-5.5% through FY2029, synergies reach the reported ~$1.5B run-rate and margins expand to 19.8% EBITDA (EBITA ~19%, Publicis-level). The buyback retires a large part of the merger share issuance at single-digit multiples and the stock re-rates toward a 14x FCF exit. Growth and margin are now tracking this path for a quarter or two; it still needs both to persist through a harder comparison and a re-rating on top, which is why the weight stays at 20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The merger scales up the problem rather than solving it: AI-native creative and self-serve media tools and advertiser in-housing erode the intermediary role, client conflicts across the combined roster force resignations, and talent leaves with the retired DDB/FCB/MullenLowe brands and the September 2026 change at the head of the advertising unit. Revenue declines 1-2% a year from FY2028, synergies are given back in pricing, EBITDA margin drifts to 15%, and the exit multiple is 9x FCF. Leverage (2.3x, 3.5x covenant) stays serviceable but roughly $400M a year of net interest is fixed against a shrinking EBITDA, and the $5B buyback is in hindsight capital spent on a melting asset. Weighted 25%, down from 30%: the near-term integration-failure route into this case has narrowed, the structural route has not.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the combined Omnicom-IPG entity on a normalised FY2026 Core Operations run-rate, not on FY2025 GAAP (one month of IPG, $1.25B of repositioning charges, negative net income) or on the pre-merger standalone history. Unlevered owner FCF is built from an adjusted-EBITA-plus-depreciation margin with SBC expensed and the share count held flat, acquired-intangible amortisation ignored as non-cash and non-deductible, operating leases left inside operating cost, and three debt-like claims deducted in the bridge: net debt, non-controlling interests and the unpaid cash severance. Cash integration costs are charged in the FY2027-28 margins rather than adjusted away. The higher post-merger leverage shows up in three places and only once each: the $6.2B net debt in the bridge, the 29% debt weight and BBB+ marginal cost in WACC, and the bear case's fixed interest burden against shrinking EBITDA. The three scenarios carry the integration and structural-decline risk in their flows and weights; WACC is the same 8.75% in all three so that risk is charged once. Terminal value is capped at 9-14x FCF, below the sector's pre-2022 multiples, because the market's single-digit P/E is itself evidence that a Gordon-growth exit is not something a buyer has to grant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Integration durability: the Q3 2026 print removed the near-term failure case, but client defections or talent attrition after the network consolidation and the advertising-unit leadership change would show up as organic growth falling below the 2-3% industry rate in 2027 and would move the base case toward the bear path
Structural AI disintermediation: if self-serve platforms and in-housing compress agency revenue faster than the bear case's -1 to -2% a year, the 15% bear margin and 9x cap are not the floor

Synergy give-back: the base margin path now assumes ~18.0% mature EBITA, roughly the Q3 2026 Core level; competitive pricing or reinvestment could hold the full-year margin nearer the ~17.4% FY2026E level

Discount rate: the 10-year Treasury has held near 5% since September; the 75bp WACC correction in this update is the largest single item in the reconciliation bridge, and the terminal caps (not Gordon) set the terminal value, so further rate moves act through discounting alone
Terminal multiple: the 12x base cap sits above today's ~10.5x EV/owner-FCF; if the market never re-rates, intrinsic value is overstated by roughly the gap between the two multiples on the FY2036 FCF

Leverage and rates: 2.3x covenant leverage with ~$10B of debt and net interest expense running near $400M a year (up from ~$170M pre-merger); a cyclical ad downturn would cut FCF while the remaining $2.1B of buyback authorization and the $0.80 quarterly dividend are being funded, and the EUR500M 0.80% notes due 2027 refinance at a far higher coupon

Disposal proceeds and remaining restructuring cash are both estimates: remaining proceeds are carried at zero (upside), the $229.5M severance liability at book (could rise if further actions are announced), and rent on exited real estate is covered only by the FY2027-28 margin haircut
FTC consent order and five-year compliance monitor add a compliance cost and client-relationship friction not separately modelled

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E Core Operations revenue (net of dispositions and held-for-sale businesses), combined Omnicom+IPG. Anchored to nine-month 2026 Core Operations revenue of $17,621.4M (Q3 2026 10-Q: +7.1% vs combined 9M 2025, 5.8% organic; Q3 alone $6,010.7M, 7.2% organic) grossed up on a ~72.6% nine-month seasonal share (Omnicom standalone 72.4% in FY2023 and FY2024, nudged up because the maintained ~5% full-year organic guidance implies Q4 organic growth of only ~3%). Prior version: 24,100 off H1. FY2025 reported revenue of $17,271.9M carries only ~5 weeks of IPG and is NOT the base; FY2024 and earlier describe the pre-merger standalone company. Reported 9M 2026 revenue of $19,228.2M includes $1,606.8M from disposed and held-for-sale businesses that is excluded here.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 272,847,468 shares on the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (2026-10-20) plus 1.4M dilutive options and restricted shares (Q3 2026 weighted diluted 275.4M less basic 274.0M). 6.0M anti-dilutive options and restricted shares are excluded per the filing's own table. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $5.0B post-merger buyback ($3,210.3M of repurchase cash in 9M 2026 incl. the $2.5B ASR, settled May 2026 with 32.2M shares delivered; $2,100M of authorization remaining at end-August per the 10-Q repurchase table, completion targeted April 2027) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 September 2026 10-Q: long-term debt including current portion $9,957.8M + short-term debt $60.5M = $10,018.3M total debt; cash and cash equivalents $3,796.4M. Net debt $6,221.9M ties exactly to the MD&A net-debt table. No commercial paper or revolver drawings outstanding at quarter-end. Finance leases and operating lease liabilities are excluded from debt -- see lease_treatment. Note the seasonal pattern: operating capital used $2.3B in 9M 2026 and normally reverses in Q4, so quarter-end net debt is above the year-end level; no credit is taken for that.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2026E estimate, levered, GAAP: adjusted net income ~$2.9B (guided high-teens growth on the $8.65 2025 base; Q3 2026 adjusted diluted EPS $2.73, +21.9%) less after-tax amortization, integration and repositioning costs (~$600M), plus D&A ~$670M and SBC ~$112M, less capex ~$235M, working capital assumed neutral = reported FCF ~$2,850M. Left at the prior estimate: nine-month OCF of $37.8M carries the $2.3B seasonal operating-capital outflow and says nothing about the full year. Owner FCF = 2,850 - 150 (SBC incl. withholding) - 134 (interest income) = 2,566. NOTE: the engine projects UNLEVERED owner FCF from EBITDA, so its FY2027 figure sits ~$300M above last_fcf by the after-tax net interest expense that last_fcf still carries (net interest expense $269.5M in 9M 2026, guided just under $100M for Q4); the debt cost is charged through WACC and the net-debt bridge, not the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement share-based compensation $83.3M for 9M 2026 (annualised ~$112M); FY2025 10-K $100.8M (Omnicom standalone + 5 weeks IPG), FY2024 $91.4M. Withholding on net-share settlement: 14,695 + 141,080 + 274,585 = 430,360 shares withheld in Q1-Q3 2026 (Item 2 of each 10-Q), ~$34M at ~$80, taken as ~$38M for the year. No company-published combined figure, so the two lines are summed: $150M = 0.62% of Core revenue. The prior version carried only ~$10M of withholding (one quarter's count read as a year's).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026E ~$134M (9M 2026 $105.5M, Q3 $28.6M). inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 66.33-89.57
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 5.07% (10y UST, ^TNX regular close 2026-11-18; it has held 4.9-5.3% since early September), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~10.6%; pre-tax marginal cost of debt ~6.2% (BBB+/Baa1, ~110bp over the 10y; the in-place coupon book is cheaper, but WACC prices the marginal dollar) x (1-26%) = 4.6%; capital structure ~71% equity (~$24.2B market cap) / 29% debt ($10.0B gross) -> 8.8%, set at 8.75%. LEVERAGE: the merger took gross debt from $6.1B to $10.0B and covenant leverage to 2.3x (2.7x a year earlier, 3.5x ceiling); that is reflected in the 29% debt weight and the BBB+ spread, and in the net-debt bridge -- not by an extra premium, and the debt weight is not allowed to pull WACC down further than the market-value mix does. CHANGE FROM PRIOR: 8.0% -> 8.75%. The prior build used a 4.2% risk-free rate that was already ~100bp stale on its own valuation date (the 10y was ~5.2% on 2026-10-02); this is a correction of an input, not a new view on risk. The same rate is used in all three scenarios: structural-decline and integration risk are charged ONCE, in the bear scenario's flows and its weight, not again through the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Omnicom is a US GAAP filer whose operating-lease cost (occupancy and other costs $1.5B in 9M 2026 incl. the IPG footprint) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path. Operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is depreciation only (0.85% of Core revenue; 9M 2026 depreciation and ROU-asset amortisation line $144.6M = 0.75% of total reported revenue), excluding acquired-intangible amortisation ($355.2M in 9M 2026, ~$475M/yr), which is non-cash and, for the stock-for-stock IPG deal, largely non-deductible: it is neither deducted from EBITDA nor added back. KNOWN GAP: real-estate exit charges ($86.1M non-cash in 9M 2026) impair space whose rent is still payable; that residual rent no longer runs through adjusted EBITA and is covered only by the integration-cost haircut on the FY2027-28 margins.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests $375.1M (equity) + redeemable NCI $266.9M at 30-Sep-2026 = $642.0M deducted from enterprise value (down from $929.2M at 30-Jun: $288.5M of cash was paid in 9M 2026 to buy in minorities, which is already in net debt). Flows are left unattributed (NCI's profit share $52.8M in 9M 2026, ~$70-75M/yr; capitalised at ~10% that is ~$700-750M, so the balance-sheet deduction is now slightly BELOW the capitalised claim rather than above it -- a ~$0.3/share understatement of the deduction, noted and not adjusted).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) via make build-dcf -- Omnicom is an operating services company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; routing row 2 of dcf-methods/SKILL.md (cyclical operating company); owner-fcf-adaptations rules applied for leases, NCI and charging risk once. Same model as the 2026-10-02 valuation; no memory entry for this ticker. THIS IS AN UPDATE on the Q3 2026 10-Q and the 2026-10-22 results -- see reconciliation. MERGER NORMALISATION: the IPG all-stock acquisition closed 2025-11-26, so FY2024 and earlier are a different (standalone) entity and FY2025 is a transition year (-$54.5M net income on ~$1.25B of Q4 repositioning charges; shares 196M -> 313M; debt $6.1B -> $9.3B). fy0 is therefore FY2026E on the company's own Core Operations basis; the explicit horizon runs FY2027-FY2036. EBITDA margin = adjusted EBITA margin (Core: H1 2026 16.4%, Q3 18.2%, nine months ~17.0%, FY2026E ~17.4% with a seasonally strong Q4 and guided +200-210bp for the year) plus depreciation ~0.8pp = ~18.2% FY2026E; the FY2027 and FY2028 base-case margins are haircut ~0.7pp and ~0.3pp for residual cash integration, repositioning and exited-lease costs (9M 2026: $135.8M repositioning plus integration and transaction costs, ~$276M gross before a $72.5M disposal gain), so the paths are after those costs, not 'adjusted'. The $229.5M of unpaid cash severance and contract-termination liabilities at 30-Sep-2026 is a debt-like claim deducted in the equity bridge. Held-for-sale businesses still have NEGATIVE net assets (assets $490.8M vs liabilities $684.7M), so remaining disposal proceeds are carried at zero; $413.9M of proceeds received in 9M 2026 is already in cash. Working capital is modelled as neutral (wc_capture 0): media payables exceed receivables so growth has historically been cash-neutral-to-positive over a cycle, but FY2022-FY2024 saw $170-500M/yr of outflows and no capture is credited. Cash tax 26% = the reported nine-month 2026 effective rate (26.0%, flattered slightly by favourable settlements of uncertain tax positions; $538.3M of income taxes paid in 9M), applied to unlevered EBIT. Buybacks beyond the SBC offset are value-neutral under the flat-count convention even though at a single-digit adjusted P/E they would be accretive; that upside is deliberately not modelled. The CSV FY2025 EBITDA (721.4) and net income (-54.5) are post-charge GAAP figures and are not used as a base. SYNERGY TARGET: the Analysis reports the run-rate target raised to ~$1.5B from secondary press; only the company-confirmed $900M for 2026 is relied on in the base case, the $1.5B sits in the bull case. The Analysis's '~$1.8B buyback authorization remaining' differs from the 10-Q repurchase table ($2,100M at end-August); the 10-Q governs.

bear.rationale: UNCHANGED paths (growth, margin, 9x cap). The structural-decline branch: AI-native self-serve platforms and client in-housing shrink the agency intermediary role, merger client conflicts and talent attrition bite, revenue declines 1-2%/yr from FY2028, synergies are consumed by pricing pressure so EBITDA margin drifts back to 15% (below the pre-merger combined level), 9x exit cap. One strong integration quarter is evidence against the execution leg of this case, which is why its weight came down, but says nothing about the structural leg, which is why its path did not move. What would move it: two or more years of positive organic growth with stable margin after the synergy programme has run off.

base.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED: FY2027 3.0% then fading to 2.5%. The 7.2% Q3 2026 organic print and 5.8% nine-month rate are captured in the higher FY2026E base, not extrapolated: management kept ~5% for the year citing limited Q4 project visibility, the 2025 IPG comparison was soft, and the long-run holding-company organic rate is 2-3%. What would move it: FY2027 organic guidance (due with Q4 results in February 2027) at or above 4%, or a second consecutive quarter above 6% on a harder comparison. No FX credited.
base.margin_rationale: CHANGED (was 17.6 / 18.2 / 18.5 mature). FY2026E Core adjusted EBITA is now tracking ~17.4% (nine months ~17.0%, Q3 18.2%, +200bp y/y, full-year guided +200-210bp) against the ~16.8% the prior version assumed, i.e. ~18.2% EBITDA already. FY2027 underlying 18.7% (the rest of the $900M 2026 synergy annualising) less ~0.7pp residual cash integration, repositioning and exited-lease cost = 18.0%; FY2028 underlying 18.9% less 0.3pp = 18.6%; mature 18.8% EBITDA = ~18.0% EBITA, just under the Q3 2026 Core level and between Omnicom's standalone 15.5-16% and Publicis' ~19-20%. Mature margin is raised only 0.3pp: some of the synergy is assumed given back in pricing and reinvestment.
base.sbc_rationale: CHANGED 0.5% -> 0.6%: FY2026E SBC plus withholding is $150M (0.62% of Core revenue) once all three quarters' withheld-share counts are included.
base.terminal_rationale: UNCHANGED: the 12x FCF cap binds (Gordon at 8.75%/2% would be 15.1x). 12x is below Omnicom's own 2015-2021 EV/owner-FCF range (~12-14x) and above today's ~10.5x on FY2027E unlevered owner FCF; a lower cap is used because the business is cyclical and structurally slower-growing.

bull.rationale: Synergies reach the reported ~$1.5B run-rate and the scale/data platform (Omni + Acxiom/Kinesso) wins share: organic growth holds 4-5.5% through FY2029, EBITDA margin 19.8% (EBITA ~19%, Publicis-level), 14x exit cap (still below the sector's pre-2022 multiples). CHANGED: only the first three margin years (was 18.0 / 19.0 / 19.5), lifted so the ramp starts from the ~18.2% FY2026E level now in evidence; the 19.8% mature margin, growth path and cap are UNCHANGED.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: CHANGED from 30/50/20. Bear 25% (house default 15%): the prior 30% rested partly on an integration 'unproven for at least four more quarters'; Q3 2026 delivered 7.2% organic growth, +200bp of margin, leverage down to 2.3x and management calling integration nearly complete, which removes part of the execution tail, but the structural AI-disintermediation question and a cyclical ad market with limited Q4 visibility remain. Base 55%: the five points released from the bear go here. Bull held at 20% (house default 35%): it still needs sustained 4-5% growth, a Publicis-level margin and a re-rating to all land, and one or two quarters on a soft comparison do not establish the first of those.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
